# Hub **Hub** is a central hub that your AI agent harnesses connect to. Each harness (a coding agent's terminal app, server or IDE plugin) runs a thin client, a *spoke*, that connects outbound to your hub; the hub gives you one place to follow, steer and be notified about every agent session on every machine, from your phone or any browser. Hub is harness-agnostic by design: the hub's API, web console and spoke protocol are not tied to one agent. [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) is the first supported harness, through the `@huynle/hub` OpenCode plugin; Claude Code, Codex and terminal agents described by a preset connect through spokes of their own ([docs/harnesses.md](docs/harnesses.md)). More harnesses can connect by speaking the same spoke protocol (`packages/protocol`), most easily on the spoke SDK ([docs/spoke-sdk.md](docs/spoke-sdk.md)). | Harness | Connect it with | Evidence | What the hub can do | |---|---|---|---| | OpenCode | `opencode plugin add @huynle/hub` | native | everything below | | Claude Code | `hub claude [claude args…]` | hooks | follow, message, answer permissions, stop; launches | | Codex | `hub codex [codex args…]` | rpc | follow, message, turns, steer, interrupt, answer approvals, stop; launches | | Presets (Aider, goose, your own) | `hub preset run ` | screen | paste prompts and messages, Ctrl-C | The full per-harness matrix, setup, limits and threat model: [docs/harnesses.md](docs/harnesses.md). Formerly **opencode-voice** and, briefly, **opencode-hub** ([what changed](#migrating-from-opencode-voice-or-opencode-hub)). ## Features - **Remote console**: one hub connects all your agent processes and machines. Follow live activity (tool calls, thinking, subagents, streamed replies), read the conversation, send a turn (it steers the run while the session is busy), stop a whole session tree, answer permissions, switch models, and start new sessions, from the phone. - **Notifications**: web push when a session asks a question, needs permission, fails, or is **all done** (the session and all its subagents and scripts settled, once per run), plus opt-in finer kinds (every turn, stopped, retrying, each subagent, each script, long tools) and **Activity updates** (one quiet, self-replacing notification per session); one toggle per kind and device, quiet hours and per-session mute ([docs/notifications.md](docs/notifications.md)). - **Live without waste**: the console's stream resumes where it left off after a lock or app switch (event ids + replay), pauses while the page is hidden, and carries streamed text only for the session on screen. - **Running detection**: a session counts as working while OpenCode reports it busy or retrying, or while a shell or terminal it started still runs (e.g. a background `sleep 60 &` or build script), also when it was already running before the plugin started. - **Voice** (optional feature, `/voice`): dictation and a hands-free conversation mode. Voice mode always talks through a **voice front**: a hidden, fast voice agent that says what it understood and relays your request to the session, which keeps its own agent, model and tools (Settings → Voice → Voice front; on by default, off talks to the session directly). Bring your own speech: OpenRouter or any OpenAI-compatible STT/TTS service (including self-hosted). A developer **recording mode** (Settings → Voice, off by default) keeps your voice segments, transcripts, replies and timing on the hub for 7 days, private to you, with Export and Delete ([docs/voice-recording.md](docs/voice-recording.md)). - **What's open in your terminals first**: sessions open in Herdr or the OpenCode TUI, grouped like Herdr's sidebar, with the rest under Recent; rename, pin and archive in sync across devices. - **Fork and revert a message** (OpenCode): hover one of your messages for Copy, Fork (a new session with the conversation before it, the message in its composer) and Revert (hide it and what follows, restore the files the session changed, edit and resend; Restore undoes it) ([docs/session-view.md](docs/session-view.md#fork-and-revert-a-message)). - **Agent identity**: every session's shells carry its own hub identity, so an agent can run `hub status`, name itself (`@scout`), claim a role (`@@reviewer`) and read other sessions, with app tokens for scripts and device tokens for apps ([Agent identity](#agent-identity-agent-api)). - **Agent messaging**: sessions, scripts and you message each other through the hub (`hub msg @reviewer …`, `hub ask`, the OpenCode `hub` tool, `/msg`, `hub mcp`); asks to `@me` become Decisions you answer from the console ([Agent messaging](#agent-messaging)). - **Session subscriptions**: a session follows others (`hub subscribe @builder --type state:idle`, a role, a `#team` or its subagents) and gets one batched hub message per window to react to, waking it when idle, with loop protection and rate limits ([docs/subscriptions.md](docs/subscriptions.md)). - **Launches**: you, a script or an app start a session on one of your machines (`hub launch --branch feat/x --prompt "…"`): a `hub node` daemon prepares a git worktree, the session gets its name, roles, labels and first prompt, and ends by itself when it is done, with signed webhooks for apps ([docs/launches.md](docs/launches.md)). Test an app against a real hub with simulated machines: the app fixture ([docs/app-integration-testing.md](docs/app-integration-testing.md)). - **More harnesses**: Claude Code (`hub claude`, through its hooks), Codex (`hub codex`, through its app-server) and any terminal agent described by a data-only preset (`hub preset run`); the console shows only the controls each harness's spoke serves, with an evidence badge and honest delivery labels ([docs/harnesses.md](docs/harnesses.md)). Write a spoke for another harness on the spoke SDK and check it with the conformance suite ([docs/spoke-sdk.md](docs/spoke-sdk.md)). - **Workspaces and supervision**: group sessions from any machine into a durable workspace, drag them under a master or supervisor (separate from native subagent ancestry), track explicit assignments on a situation board, replace a master explicitly, and keep supervisors informed with batched digests and durable checkpoints ([docs/workspaces.md](docs/workspaces.md)). - **Split panes and side chats**: up to 4 sessions or artifacts side by side, and side chats started from a bounded copy of a session that never interrupt it ([docs/workspaces.md](docs/workspaces.md#side-chats)). - **Agent profiles**: shared, versioned instructions, skills and commands, pinned to a session, launch or team role at runtime, with an honest per-harness acknowledgment ([docs/profiles.md](docs/profiles.md)). - **Artifacts with AI**: persistent, revisioned documents, tables, charts, dashboards and files in an **Artifacts** library. AI jobs ask about or edit them through an agent you choose, and interactive apps run only in an isolated sandbox host ([docs/artifacts.md](docs/artifacts.md), [docs/artifact-host.md](docs/artifact-host.md)). - **Teams**: roles, an entry role that takes work, and enforced one-way or two-way communication paths (or open mode), staffed with sessions from any machine. The console's **Teams** page lists them and shows each team's members, work (live intake status) and communication ([docs/teams.md](docs/teams.md), [intake](docs/teams-intake.md)). - **Watchtower** (formerly Bird's-eye view): a 3D, 2D or list picture of machines, sessions, teams and live message flow, with a team editor ([docs/watchtower.md](docs/watchtower.md)). - **Media in sessions**: tool screenshots, attachments and image files a reply names show in the transcript (with a full-screen viewer), Mermaid diagrams draw, HTML blocks and local pages preview in the isolated host, and web images and link previews load through the hub for sites you allow, without loosening the console's CSP ([docs/session-view.md](docs/session-view.md#media-in-sessions), security: [docs/media-security.md](docs/media-security.md)). - **Session details**: context usage, todos, MCP status, branch and per-file diffs, on demand; unread marks synced per user. - **Self-hostable**: a hub on your computer with nothing extra to install, or your own hub for phones anywhere (standalone binary, Docker or Bun), with single-owner pairing or sign-in with Google for several people. In a harness, `/hub` configures the harness's connection to the hub, and each feature is its own `/`: today `/voice`, `/who` and `/msg`; more features will be added the same way. Requires OpenCode v2 (tested with 2.0.25) for the OpenCode harness; the Claude Code spoke is tested with Claude Code 2.1.296 and the Codex spoke with Codex 0.160.0. The hub runs on OpenCode's own runtime, a standalone binary, Docker, or [Bun](https://bun.sh) ≥ 1.3. ## Quick start (OpenCode) Install the plugin (adds it to your global OpenCode config), then restart the background service so it loads: ```sh opencode plugin add @huynle/hub opencode service restart ``` OpenCode 2.x loads plugins per project, on the first request that opens one, and has no hook at server start: a freshly (re)started background service or `opencode serve` has no hub connection, so its machine shows **offline** until a client (the TUI, the web app) opens a project. OpenCode also unloads a project after an hour without session activity, and the hub plugin with it. `hub node` ([launches](docs/launches.md#hub-node)) keeps the background service warm by itself (cheap location reads every 30 s), and any foreground `opencode serve` you list in node.json: ```json { "workspaceRoots": ["/Users/you/projects"], "opencode": { "servers": [{ "url": "http://127.0.0.1:4096", "passwordFile": "/Users/you/.config/hub/opencode-4096.pw" }] } } ``` (the server's `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` in a `chmod 600` file; loopback URLs only). To stop OpenCode unloading projects at all, set `"experimental": { "location_idle_timeout": false }` in your OpenCode config (or a longer duration such as `"8 hours"`). Without `hub node`, open OpenCode once, or send the read yourself, e.g. for a foreground `opencode serve --port 4096` with `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` set: `curl -fsS -u "opencode:$OPENCODE_PASSWORD" http://127.0.0.1:4096/api/agent >/dev/null`. Which sessions show **online**: the background service reports all of its recent sessions; a foreground `opencode serve` with `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` (or `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD`) in its environment reports every recent session of the projects it has loaded, idle ones included (so hub messages reach them at once); a TUI's own server, or a foreground server started without a password in its environment (OpenCode then makes one up the plugin cannot read), reports only the sessions that were active in that process. Install from npm: the npm package ships the built web app, so the plugin can run a local hub. A GitHub install (`opencode plugin add github:huynle/hub`) has no built web app (`web/dist` is not in the repository): it works for connecting to a hub that runs elsewhere, but it does not start a local hub (`/hub` → **Start local hub** and the automatic start say the web app is missing; a hub started by hand from such an install answers 503 on its pages). To run a hub yourself, use the npm package, a [release binary](#running-the-hub) or Docker, or run `npm install && npm run build:web` in a source checkout. Then, in OpenCode: | Command | What it does | |---|---| | **`/hub`** | Configures this harness's hub connection: the server URL, connect and approve (enroll) this machine, which sessions to share (mode), pair a phone, and open the hub in the browser. The first time it offers **Set up Hub** with two paths (below). | | **`/voice`** | The Voice feature: talks to the session on screen. It connects (running the setup first when needed), shares the session for Voice and opens it in the browser with Voice mode starting. | | **`/who [project \| #team \| @@role]`** | Lists the sessions the hub shows the session on screen: every online one (named or not; an unnamed one by its ID and title) and the named or role-holding ones while offline, with project, state, online and roles. A `You: @name · project` line heads the dialog (`You: ses_… (unnamed…)` until it has a name: ask the agent to name itself, or run `hub name @name --session ses_…` in a logged-in terminal; a `!` command gets no session token), its own row is marked `(you)` and listed first, then online before offline. | | **`/msg @name text`** | Sends the text word for word to another session (`@name`, `@@role`, `@name.project`, `ses_…`, or `@me` for you) as the session on screen. Needs a shared, connected session. | ### Local: everything on this computer 1. `/hub` → **On this computer (local — nothing to install)**. The plugin starts a hub in the background, connects this machine (a fresh local hub approves it by itself), shares every session ("On this computer, only sessions I choose" shares only sessions you switch on), and opens the hub in your browser with a one-time sign-in link. 2. Use it: open any session to follow and steer it. For Voice, set up speech once (Settings → Speech): pick a provider and paste its API key (one [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/keys) key covers both directions, or point both at your own OpenAI-compatible servers), **Save**, then **Test voice**. Keys stay on this computer in `~/.local/state/hub`. 3. **`/voice`** in a session opens it in the browser with Voice mode (the hands-free loop) starting; `/hub` → **Open hub in browser** opens the home page any time. ### Your own hub (phones anywhere) Phones need HTTPS (for the microphone and push), so for phone use away from this computer, run the hub on a server behind your HTTPS reverse proxy (see [Running the hub](#running-the-hub)), then: 1. Open `https:///pair` in the browser you will approve from and enter the 6-digit code from the hub's log (first device only; later devices get codes from `/hub` → **Pair a phone**). 2. `/hub` → **Connect to a hub…** → `https://hub.example.com`. The plugin checks the hub answers, then opens its approve page: check the code and approve this machine. OpenCode notices the approval and asks which sessions to share (default: all). 3. On each further machine: `/hub` → **Connect to a hub…** again. Add phones with `/hub` → **Pair a phone**. Pre-configured machines: with `"server": "https://hub.example.com"` in `~/.config/hub/config.json`, `/hub` leads with **Connect to hub.example.com**. `/hub` → **Server** → **Set up again…** switches between local and a hosted hub later. Recommended for Voice mode: put the voice front on a fast, paid model in `~/.config/hub/config.json`: `"voiceModel": "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5"` (any `provider/model` you have; a session's Voice model in the console wins). # @huynle/hub-voice-client

Hub's hands-free voice loop as a package: an always-on microphone with on-device speech detection (Silero VAD),
optional end-of-turn detection (Smart Turn v3), speculative per-segment transcription, endpointing, voice commands
("stop", "pause listening"), sentence-by-sentence speech of the agent's replies with barge-in, and progress cues
(earcons and short phrases). The Hub console's Voice mode is built on it; other web apps can embed the same loop.

Internal workspace package (`private`, not published on its own). The console imports it from source
(`packages/voice-client/src`); an app that does not build it from source uses the standalone build (below).

## The transport

Everything the loop sends to or hears from its session goes through a `VoiceTransport`, the interface frozen by the
app-front contract (`docs/plans/2026-11-08-app-front-contracts.md` §7, `packages/protocol/src/app-front.ts`):

```ts
interface VoiceTransport {
  conversation(on: boolean, options?: { front?: boolean }): Promise<{ on: boolean; front?: boolean }>
  utterance(text: string): Promise<{ inboxID: string }>
  interrupt(): Promise<void>
  transcribe(audio: Blob, options?: { signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<{ text: string }>
  speak(text: string, options?: { signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<ReadableStream<Uint8Array>> // audio/mpeg
  events(listener: (event: VoiceEvent) => void): () => void // say | heard | conversation | status | reset
}
```

- **The package never holds a Hub token and never calls the Hub.** The console's transport
  (`web/src/voice/console-transport.ts`) uses its cookie routes and SSE; an app's transport calls **its own server**,
  which keeps the app's Hub credentials and proxies to `/api/agent/speech/*` and `/api/agent/sessions/:addr/*`
  (contract §4, §5). **`appTransport({base})`** is that app transport, ready made (below).
- `events` delivers the session's `say`, `heard` and `conversation` events (and, from an app stream, `status` and
  `reset`: a `reset` drops the replies still to speak). `VoiceEvents` is a small multicast source for transports that
  push events in.
- A transport may accept more than the contract (`VoiceClientTransport`: a `keepalive` for the page-hide
  `conversation(false)`, request `headers` for the recording plug-in, `agent` in the answer); every plain
  `VoiceTransport` is accepted.

### `appTransport`: the app's own server

```ts
import { appTransport } from "@huynle/hub-voice-client"
const transport = appTransport({ base: `/hub/voice/sessions/${sessionID}`, onEnd: (reason) => console.log(reason) })
```

It calls six routes under `base` on the page's origin, with the page's own cookie (`credentials: "same-origin"`, or
your `fetch`): `POST {base}/conversation {on, front?}`, `POST {base}/utterance {text}`, `POST {base}/interrupt`,
`POST {base}/transcribe` (the raw audio, its type as `Content-Type`), `POST {base}/speak {text}` (audio/mpeg back) and
`GET {base}/stream` (the hub's app stream, relayed as SSE). Your server proxies them to the hub with the user's token
(the reference: `examples/app-front-bff`). `events` opens one relayed stream for all listeners, maps `say`, `heard`,
`conversation`, `status` and `reset`, and resumes with `Last-Event-ID` after a drop or `end` `slow`/`token_expired`,
with exponential backoff (jittered, capped; `reconnectDelayMs`, `maxReconnectDelayMs`). A stream that closes without
progress counts as a failure; `end` `revoked`/`grant`/`gone`, a 4xx from your server, or `maxReconnects` (5)
failures in a row stop it (`onEnd(reason)`, `unavailable` for the last). Refusals throw
`AppTransportError {status, code?, retryAfter?}` (the hub's envelope passed through).

### Your own transport

```ts
import { Conversation, VoiceEvents, sharedPlayer, unlockAudio } from "@huynle/hub-voice-client"

const events = new VoiceEvents() // fed from your server's relay of the session's stream
const transport = {
  conversation: (on, o) => post(`/my/voice/conversation`, { on, ...o }),
  utterance: (text) => post(`/my/voice/utterance`, { text }),
  interrupt: () => post(`/my/voice/interrupt`, {}),
  transcribe: async (audio) => (await fetch("/my/voice/transcribe", { method: "POST", body: audio })).json(),
  speak: async (text, o) => (await fetch("/my/voice/speak", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ text }), signal: o?.signal })).body!,
  events: (listener) => events.subscribe(listener),
}
unlockAudio() // inside the tap that starts Voice
const conversation = new Conversation({ sessionID, transport, player: sharedPlayer(), ui, options: { front: () => true } })
await conversation.start()
```

`ui` (`ConversationUI`) receives the loop's state, mic level, user and agent bubbles, notes and the turn timing.
`VoiceController` and `VoiceNotifier` (one Voice session at a time, the "Voice mode on" notification) are optional
app-level helpers.

## Assets, workers and the standalone build

`loadSilero()` and `loadSmartTurn()` start module workers (`silero-worker.ts`, `smart-turn-worker.ts`) that run
onnxruntime-web's single-threaded wasm build (no SharedArrayBuffer, so no COOP/COEP headers) on the bundled models.
They and the AudioWorklet are loaded with `new URL(…, import.meta.url)`, which Vite (and other bundlers that support
the pattern) emits as hashed files; the models are `?url` imports in the workers.

The package has no dependencies of its own: building it needs `onnxruntime-web` 1.23.2 (the root
devDependencies' version), and a Vite-compatible bundler when built from source.

`npm run build:voice-client` (root) builds `packages/voice-client/dist/` for apps that do not bundle the sources:

- `index.js`: the package as one ES module (the exports of `src/index.ts`);
- `assets/`: the two workers, onnxruntime-web's `.wasm` (12 MB, compresses to ~3 MB), the two `.onnx` models
  (Silero VAD 2.3 MB, Smart Turn 8.7 MB) and the AudioWorklet, hashed and referenced relative to `index.js`;
- `licenses/`: the models' licence files.

Serve `dist/` from the page's own origin (module workers and worklets must be same-origin) and cache `assets/` for
good (the names are content-hashed).

## Content-Security-Policy for embedding apps

The page's policy needs, beyond the app's usual sources:

```
worker-src 'self';         # the two module workers (same-origin files; blob: and data: are not needed)
script-src 'self';         # the AudioWorklet module (addModule) and the package's chunks
connect-src 'self';        # the workers fetch the .wasm and .onnx files; your transport calls your server
media-src 'self' blob:;    # replies and cues play from blob: URLs (MediaSource or whole clips)
```

**wasm and workers.** onnxruntime-web compiles its wasm inside the workers. A worker runs under the policy sent with
**its own script** (not the page's): when your server sends no CSP on `assets/*-worker-*.js` (the console's sends its
policy with the HTML only), nothing more is needed. When it sends one on every response (many frameworks do), that
policy must allow `script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` and `connect-src 'self'`, or speech detection silently falls
back to the energy detector and Smart Turn to the timers. Nothing is inlined, no `eval`, no CORS.

The console's own policy is `src/central/csp.ts`; `web/e2e/voice-smart-turn.ts` and `web/e2e/voice-recording.ts` run the
loop under it, enforced.

# hub sandbox image

What an OpenShell sandbox of `hub node` runs (design §6.4, decision lk6gn3u7, spike report gut64rwq): Debian
bookworm-slim with git, bash, ca-certificates, curl and procps, the pinned Linux OpenCode
(`@opencode/cli-linux-<arch>@OPENCODE_VERSION` from npm, checked against the registry's sha512), the hub plugin
(this repository's package, installed with its production dependencies) and two scripts.

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `image.ts` | Names, layout and the commands the runtime and `build.ts` run (pure) |
| `build.ts` | Stages the layout, builds the image (`docker build`), or packs the bootstrap tarball |
| `Dockerfile` | The image, built from the staged context only |
| `start.sh` → `bin/hub-sandbox-start` | Starts the entry detached (`setsid nohup`, log `.hub/harness.log`) and returns |
| `entry.sh` → `bin/hub-sandbox-entry` | Waits for the start op, runs and supervises `opencode serve --service` |

## Layout

The same under both roots, so one entry script serves both:

```
<root>/bin/opencode                       IMAGE_ROOT     = /usr/local          (the image)
<root>/bin/hub-sandbox-start              BOOTSTRAP_ROOT = /sandbox/.hub/opt   (the upload fallback)
<root>/bin/hub-sandbox-entry
<root>/lib/hub/node_modules/@huynle/hub   the plugin
```

## Contract with the runtime

1. Create the sandbox **without a main command** (it stays Ready; a main command that ends moves it to Completed and
   exec is refused).
2. Exec `startCommand(root)` (`/usr/local/bin/hub-sandbox-start`) at any point; it returns at once and a second call
   does nothing while the entry runs.
3. Upload `.hub/config.json` (`{hubURL, token, launchID}`, read by the plugin's spoke, never by the scripts),
   optionally `.hub/env.json` (a JSON object of extra variables), then touch `.hub/ready`. The entry waits for both
   `config.json` and `ready`.
4. The entry sets `OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH/AUTOUPDATE/PROJECT_CONFIG=1`, `XDG_*_HOME=/sandbox/.xdg/*`,
   `HUB_LAUNCH_CONFIG`, a random `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` unless given, and writes the global OpenCode config loading the
   plugin. `env.json` cannot override those, `PATH`, `HOME`, `BUN_*`/`LD_*` or OpenShell's CA variables
   (`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, `SSL_CERT_FILE`, …), which are kept as OpenShell injected them: Bun trusts the proxy CA only
   through them. An invalid `env.json` ends the entry with status 2.
5. It runs `opencode serve --service --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4096` in `/sandbox/work` (else `/sandbox`) and sends
   one authorized request so the server loads its instance and the plugin.
6. `.hub/stop` holding `graceful` (SIGTERM, SIGKILL after `HUB_STOP_GRACE`, 10 s) or `kill` (SIGKILL) stops it;
   `.hub/exited` then holds the exit code. `.hub/entry.pid` and `.hub/harness.pid` exist while they run.

## Publishing (deliberate, not automated)

OpenShell's vm driver does **not** use local Docker images: it pulls from an **HTTPS registry** (a plain-http local
registry is refused, rootfs tarballs need the gateway's `allow_driver_config`, and local images only work when the
gateway itself sees a container engine through `DOCKER_HOST` or `/var/run/docker.sock`, an operator choice). To use the
image, publish it, for example:

```sh
bun packages/runtime-openshell/image/build.ts image --arch arm64 --tag ghcr.io/<owner>/hub-sandbox:<tag>
docker push ghcr.io/<owner>/hub-sandbox:<tag>   # or a multi-arch manifest built per architecture
```

and point the node at it (`openshell.profiles.<name>.image` in node.json, or the runtime's default image).

## Upload fallback (gateways that cannot pull the image)

On the gateway's default image (`nvcr.io/nvidia/base/ubuntu:24.04`; `/usr` read-only), the runtime uploads the
bootstrap tarball under `/sandbox/.hub/`, runs `bootstrapCommands(uploaded)` (unpack into `/sandbox/.hub/opt`, remove
the tarball) and then `startCommand(BOOTSTRAP_ROOT)`. Two limits: the sandbox policy must allow
`harnessBinary(BOOTSTRAP_ROOT)` (`/sandbox/.hub/opt/bin/opencode`) instead of `/usr/local/bin/opencode`, and that
image has no git (the runtime's clone and collect need it), so the fallback needs git from elsewhere.

## The harness pin list (`harness-pins.json`)

```json
{ "schema": "hub.harness-pin-list", "version": 1,
  "pins": [ { "pin": { "harness": "opencode", "version": "…", "target": "darwin-arm64", "url": "https://…/file.zip",
                       "file": "file.zip", "size": 123, "sha256": "sha256:…", "evidence": [] },
              "review": { "by": "github-handle", "on": "2026-10-28",
                          "checked": ["upstream-release", "digest-redownloaded", "evidence-listed"] } } ] }
```

`pin` is exactly a manifest `HarnessPin`. Each pin is checked with the manifest's own rules: a supported
target, an exact version, https, a plain file name, one pin per harness and target, and only evidence that
harness can offer. On top of that, the file must be the URL's last path segment, the URL may not carry
credentials, a query or a fragment, and nothing secret-shaped may appear anywhere in the list.

The list is empty until the harness adapter tasks confirm the upstream sources (HBS-06 for OpenCode 2.x).

**Review process**

1. A pin changes only through a pull request that touches `harness-pins.json`. The reviewer is not the author.
2. The reviewer fills in `review`:
   - `by`: their GitHub handle.
   - `on`: the review date.
   - `checked`: all three checks.
     - `upstream-release`: the URL is the upstream's own release asset for exactly this version and target.
     - `digest-redownloaded`: they downloaded the file themselves and computed its size and sha256, for example
       with `curl -fsSL <url> | shasum -a 256`.
     - `evidence-listed`: `evidence` lists exactly the upstream evidence published for that file (§5 of the
       contracts doc).
3. CI validates the file (`bootstrap-release-pins.test.ts`).
   - A pin an author prepared but nobody has reviewed yet lives in `harness-pins.pending.json` (schema
     `hub.harness-pin-pending`): the same pin, with a `prepared` record (`by`, `on`, `note`) instead of `review`. The
     release job reads only `harness-pins.json` and `validatePinList` refuses the pending schema, so a pending pin is
     never signed into a release. Only the dev release (below) includes it. To promote one, the reviewer redoes the
     checks, moves the entry into `harness-pins.json` with their own `review`, and removes it from the pending file.
   - Pending today: OpenCode 2.2.0 `windows-x64` (`opencode-windows-x64-baseline.zip`, member `opencode.exe`),
     prepared 2026-11-05 by an agent. It needs the owner's review.
4. At release time, the `hubctl-sign` job downloads every pinned file again and refuses to sign on any size or
   digest mismatch. The signature never vouches for a file that nobody fetched during that release.

## The release key (decision Q5)

There is one ed25519 key, with threshold 1. The private key is the `HUB_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY` secret of the
`hubctl-release` GitHub environment. Only the `hubctl-sign` job uses that environment, and only its Sign step
sees the secret. The key is PKCS#8, either PEM or base64 DER. No key is ever committed.

A maintainer sets the key up once, on their own machine. This has not been done yet:

```sh
openssl genpkey -algorithm ed25519 -out release-key.pem      # keep it offline
HUB_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY="$(cat release-key.pem)" bun scripts/hubctl-release.ts trust-root --key-id hub-release-1 \
  > packages/cli/src/bootstrap/release/trust-root.json       # public key only; commit through a reviewed PR
gh secret set HUB_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY --env hubctl-release < release-key.pem
gh variable set HUBCTL_RELEASE --body true                   # enables the hubctl release jobs
gh variable set HUBCTL_MINIMUM_VERSION --body 0.0.0           # the security floor (optional, default 0.0.0)
```

To rotate the key, publish a version-2 trust root signed by the current key (`rotateTrustRoot`), with the old key
`retired`, or `revoked` if it was compromised. Then update `trust-root.json` and the secret.

## The release workflow (`.github/workflows/release.yml`)

The hubctl jobs are added alongside the existing jobs. They run only when `HUBCTL_RELEASE` is `true`.

1. `hubctl` (needs `test`): `scripts/build-hubctl.sh --require-trust-root` cross-compiles all five targets.
   Then it smoke-tests `linux-x64` with an empty `PATH` (no bun or node): `--version` must equal the CLI
   version, and `hub --help` must equal `hubctl --help`.
   `hubctl-windows` (needs `hubctl`, `windows-latest`) runs `hubctl-windows-x64.exe --version` (must equal the CLI
   version) and `--help` with only `System32` on `PATH`.
2. `hubctl-sign` (needs `hubctl`, environment `hubctl-release`, no npm install):
   - `manifest` re-downloads the pins and writes the body. `issuedAt` is the tagged commit's time.
   - `sign` signs the body and verifies it against `trust-root.json`. A wrong secret writes nothing.
   - `verify --dist dist` runs the installer's checks on every artifact.
3. `hubctl-publish` (needs the existing `release` job, `hubctl-sign` and `hubctl-windows`): it verifies again, then attaches
   `hubctl-*`, `hubctl-manifest.json` and `HUBCTL_SHA256SUMS` to the GitHub release.

## Verifying by hand

```sh
bun scripts/hubctl-release.ts verify --manifest hubctl-manifest.json --target linux-x64 --file hubctl-linux-x64
```

The exit code is 0 when the artifact is accepted and 11 when it is rejected: `signature_invalid`, `wrong_platform`,
`integrity_mismatch`, `downgrade_rejected` or `below_security_floor`. Pass `--installed V --installed-sha256 D`,
`--floor V` and `--allow-downgrade` to apply the downgrade policy.

## A partial release (some targets only)

`manifest`, `sign` and `verify --dist` take `--targets T,…` (e.g. `--targets linux-x64`) to list exactly the
targets a test or partial release ships. Each listed target must be built and is checked in full; an artifact for
any other target is refused. `sign` refuses a partial body unless `--targets` names the same list, so a partial
release is never signed by accident. Without `--targets`, every supported target is required.

## Testing on real machines (a dev release)

`dev` makes a throwaway release that test machines install exactly like a real one, through a hub's
`HUB_RELEASE_BASE`, without the release key:

```sh
bun scripts/hubctl-release.ts dev --targets linux-x64,windows-x64 --out /tmp/hubctl-dev
cd /tmp/hubctl-dev && python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 0.0.0.0      # or: bunx serve -l 8000 .
```

Then start the hub with `HUB_RELEASE_BASE=http://<LAN IP of the serving machine>:8000` in its environment. Plain http
is allowed only on loopback or a private-network address. Its `/install.sh` and `/install.ps1` now download from
there.

It writes into `--out`:

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `hubctl-<target>`, `hubctl-windows-x64.exe` | hubctl for each listed target, built with the dev trust root embedded. |
| `hubctl-manifest.json` | The manifest (exactly the listed targets), signed with the throwaway key. |
| `HUBCTL_SHA256SUMS` | As `sha256sum` prints it, for install.sh and install.ps1. |
| `dev-trust-root.json` | The dev trust root (public key only), for `verify --trust-root`. |

- **The key.** A fresh ed25519 key with key ID `dev-<8 hex>` is generated for each run and held only in memory. The
  private half is never written, so nothing in the served directory can sign anything. Only the binaries of that run
  trust it. A release-built hubctl rejects the dev manifest (`signature_invalid`), and a dev hubctl rejects the real
  one. Rebuild to get a new release.
- **The pins.** `harness-pins.json` plus `harness-pins.pending.json` (`--pending FILE`, or `--no-pending`). Each
  pending pin is announced on stderr. Every pinned file is downloaded again and checked, unless you pass
  `--skip-pin-download`.
- **Options.** `--release V` (default: the CLI version) and `--minimum-version V` (default `0.0.0`). The release
  must be newer than what a test machine has installed, or you need `--allow-downgrade` there.
- **Never shipped.** `dev` refuses to run when `HUB_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY` is set (the signing job), on GitHub Actions
  (`GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`), or with `--out` inside the repository's `dist/`, where release builds go.

Check a dev release by hand:

```sh
bun scripts/hubctl-release.ts verify --manifest /tmp/hubctl-dev/hubctl-manifest.json \
  --trust-root /tmp/hubctl-dev/dev-trust-root.json --dist /tmp/hubctl-dev --targets linux-x64,windows-x64
```

# Claude Code bootstrap adapter (HBS-08)

This adapter plans, installs and verifies Claude Code for `hubctl setup`. It implements contracts §3.6.1, §3.10 and
§5 of `docs/bootstrap-contracts.md`. It is a pure planner. It reaches outside itself only through injected ports,
and it never gets a shell.

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `adapter.ts` | `createClaudeAdapter` (a `HarnessAdapter`) and `planClaude`. Plans, in order: pinned `install-harness`, `select-harness-version`, `merge-config` of hub's own `config:hub/claude-code.json`, `verify-harness`. Also `discover()` and `binary()`, both through the read-only `DiscoveryProbe`. |
| `source.ts` | `createClaudeHarnessSource`, the `HarnessSource` for `installHarnessExecutor`. It streams the pinned file into the step's staging area, records the optional evidence (against the staged digest; codesign on a scratch copy written in chunks) and installs the staged binary itself as `<version>/claude`. |
| `openpgp.ts` | An in-house check of a detached OpenPGP v4 RSA signature. It verifies upstream's signed `manifest.json` against the pinned release key and needs no `gpg`. |
| `verify.ts` | The real readiness probes, `claudeReadiness` (the capability is offered only when the harness is ready) and `claudeVerifyExecutor`. |
| `ports.ts` / `node.ts` | The injected ports (`Downloader`, `ProbeRunner`, `Scratch`) and their Node defaults (`httpsDownloader`, `nodeRunner`, `tempScratch`). |
| `index.ts` | Re-exports, and `claudeExecutors`: `install-harness` and `verify-harness` for claude-code. |

## Authenticity

The mandatory check is the sha256 that hub's signed manifest pins. `installHarnessExecutor` checks it first,
through `checkHarnessEvidence`. The optional evidence is then recorded as `verified`, `unavailable` or `failed`.
Any `failed` result rejects the artifact.

- **`gpg-manifest`.** The adapter fetches `…/claude-code-releases/<v>/manifest.json`, its `.sig`, and
  `https://downloads.claude.ai/keys/claude-code.asc`. The key's fingerprint must be
  `31DDDE24DDFAB679F42D7BD2BAA929FF1A7ECACE` (`CLAUDE_SIGNING_FINGERPRINT`). The signature is a v4 RSA signature
  over a binary document, using SHA-2.
  - `verified`: the signature is good, and the signed manifest lists exactly the pinned version, checksum and size
    for this platform.
  - `failed`: the signature does not verify, the signature is malformed, or the signed manifest lists other bytes
    or another version.
  - `unavailable`: there is no signature (releases before 2.1.89), the bucket cannot be reached, the key is
    another one or a rotated one, the format is unsupported, or the pin URL is outside upstream's bucket.
- **`macos-notarization`.** This check runs on macOS only. It runs `/usr/bin/codesign --verify --strict` (fixed
  argv) on a private copy of the downloaded bytes.
  - It first checks `-R=anchor apple generic and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = "Q6L2SF6YDW"`, which means signed
    by Anthropic PBC. If this fails, the result is `failed`.
  - It then checks `-R=notarized and …`. If this passes, the result is `verified`. If it fails, the result is
    `unavailable`, because the ticket may not be confirmable offline.
  - The result is also `unavailable` when codesign is missing, when the host is not macOS, or when the target is
    Linux.

## User config and credentials

- No plan ever touches `~/.claude` or `~/.claude.json`. The existing integration loads the hub plugin with
  `--plugin-dir` (`packages/claude-code/src/wrapper.ts`).
- The only config hub edits is its own `config:hub/claude-code.json`, and only the key `/binary`. The edit is
  lossless and pinned by a precondition. A rollback removes the file, or restores it if it existed before.
- Logins are user-mediated (`claude auth login`). `provider-auth` runs `claude auth status`, reads only its exit
  code and `authMethod`, and drops the rest of the output. The child gets the user's environment minus `HUB_*` and
  `BUN_BE_BUN`. `version-exec` gets only `PATH`, `HOME` and the update switches.

## Pin template for `release/harness-pins.json` (fill in from a fresh re-download; never copy digests from here)

```json
{ "pin": { "harness": "claude-code", "version": "<exact, e.g. the stable channel's>", "target": "darwin-arm64",
           "url": "https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases/<version>/darwin-arm64/claude",
           "file": "claude", "size": <bytes>, "sha256": "sha256:<hex of the re-downloaded file>",
           "evidence": ["gpg-manifest", "macos-notarization"], "minimumVersion": "2.1.89" },
  "review": { "by": "<handle>", "on": "<date>", "checked": ["upstream-release", "digest-redownloaded", "evidence-listed"] } }
```

- Pins for `linux-x64` and `linux-arm64` list `"evidence": ["gpg-manifest"]`. Linux binaries are not codesigned.
- `minimumVersion` 2.1.89 is the first release with a signed manifest.
- `file` must be `claude`, upstream's raw binary. The `.zst` variant is refused by `unpack`.

# OpenCode harness adapter (HBS-06)

The OpenCode `HarnessAdapter` for the bootstrap (contracts §3.10, §3.6.1, §3.12.1 and §5 in
`docs/bootstrap-contracts.md`). It only imports the frozen contracts and the transaction, discovery and preview
modules. Every capability is injected.

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `config.ts` | Reads an OpenCode 2 config (JSONC) and classifies the Hub plugin entry and the `hub` MCP server: absent, registered, drift, or a refusal. It computes the exact JSON-pointer sets for the lossless merge. |
| `plan.ts` | `planOpencode` and `createOpencodeAdapter`. The pinned `install-harness` comes first, then `select-harness-version`, `merge-config` (plugin), `register-mcp-server` and `verify-harness`. The planner is pure and deterministic. |
| `verify.ts` | Real readiness probes through a fixed-argv `ProcessRunner` (no shell). `locateOpencodeBinary` finds the binary that really runs. |
| `archive.ts` | A streaming unpacker for the upstream zip and tar.gz (`../archive-stream.ts`). It accepts exactly one regular file, `opencode` (`opencode.exe` in a zip on Windows targets), streams it into the step's staging area and installs it as `bin/opencode` (`bin/opencode.exe`) with mode 0755. `unpackOpencodeArchive` is the in-memory form for small fixtures. |
| `apply.ts` | The `HarnessSource` (the pinned URL only, https only, bounded by the pinned size, streamed into the staging area), the `register-mcp-server` and `verify-harness` executors, and `httpsDownload` (the body as chunks). |
| `index.ts` | `createOpencodeHarness`, the single entry point for the integrator. |

## Behaviour

- **Install.** OpenCode is installed only from the pin in hub's verified manifest for the host's exact target, into
  `data:hub/harnesses/opencode/<version>`. That version is then made `current`.
  - An OpenCode the user installed (native, brew or npm) is kept by default (`install: "if-missing"`).
  - A hub-managed OpenCode at an older version gets the pinned version installed next to it. A newer one is never
    downgraded by planning.
  - Without a pin, a missing OpenCode is `unpinned_artifact`.
  - A pin below 2.0.0 is refused, because the Hub plugin needs OpenCode 2.
- **Config.** OpenCode 2 uses `plugins: (string | {package, options?})[]` and `mcp.servers.<name>` (from
  `@opencode/schema` 2.0.26, `config/plugin.js` and `mcp.js`). hubctl edits `config:opencode/opencode.jsonc` if it
  exists, otherwise `opencode.json`. When neither exists, it creates `opencode.json`. The config is read only if
  the snapshot lists it, and must still have the snapshot's digest, otherwise `preview_stale`.
  - **Plugin.** If the Hub plugin is absent, it is appended to `/plugins`.
    - These count as registered: an exact npm entry, an unpinned npm entry, or a custom source (a `github:huynle/hub`
      spec or a checkout named `hub`).
    - These are drift, fixed by one set on that entry (or on its `package` field only): an older pin, or the legacy
      `@huynle/opencode-voice`.
    - These are refused as `conflict`: a duplicate (including across `plugins` and the OpenCode 1 key `plugin`, or
      across both files), or a pin newer than this hubctl.
  - **MCP.** `mcp.servers.hub = {type: "local", command: [<authority>, "mcp"]}`.
    - A `hub`/`hubctl mcp` server at another path (the plugin's launcher in the state dir, or a plugin cache) is
      stale. Only its `command` is replaced; `environment`, `disabled` and other fields stay.
    - These are refused: a foreign server named `hub`, or hub's MCP server under another name.
  - **Authority.** The authority is `user-bin:hubctl` by default, or `user-bin:hub` (the same command surface). Any
    other root or name (`state:hub/bin/…`, `data:…/node_modules/…`) is refused when the adapter is built.
  - **Unparseable files.** Unparseable JSONC, or JSONC with duplicate keys, is `manual_edit_required`.
- **Symlinked configs.** The adapter plans normally. `planSetup` replaces both config actions with `symlinked-config`
  manual edits that name the dotfiles file. Nothing is written through the link.
- **Readiness.** A planned or applied install is never readiness. The three required probes are:
  - `version-exec`: `<binary> --version` must report OpenCode ≥ 2.0.0, and exactly the hub `current` version when
    hub manages the binary. The binary is hub's `current` binary, otherwise what PATH resolves to. A container shim
    is refused.
  - `provider-auth`: `<binary> models --standalone` must list at least one `provider/model`. This sends no prompt
    and costs nothing. `--standalone` runs a private server inside the probe: it tests exactly the installed binary
    and starts no background service (`opencode serve --service`). Without it the first probe started that service
    from the hub-installed version directory, where it kept running after verify; on Windows it kept that directory
    busy, so `hubctl setup rollback` could not remove it (Phase 2 end-to-end run). A stronger `ProviderProbe` can
    be injected.
  - `spoke-connected`: an injected `SpokeProbe`. Without one, the probe fails, so OpenCode is never ready by default.

  On a cold start (the first use of a directory) OpenCode 2's background service can take longer than the CLI's ~5 s
  to activate its plugins, and the CLI fails with HTTP 503 "Location plugins did not finish activating". The
  `--version` and `models` probes retry once, after 1 s, on exactly that failure (`ACTIVATION_FAILURE`, read from the
  child's output only to recognise it); any other failure is reported at once (HBS-12).

  Every probe runs through the bounded runner (`../process-tree.ts`): nothing it starts outlives it. A timeout, a
  cancel or too much output ends its whole process tree, and whatever it left running when it exited is ended too
  (POSIX: its own process group; Windows: `taskkill /T /F` from System32, and the exited probe's children found by a
  fixed CIM query).

  Details are built by the adapter, never copied from harness output. Anything that looks like a credential is
  withheld. The child process gets the user's own environment, and nothing from it is recorded.

  Contract v1.2 classifies them: `version-exec` is an integrity probe (its failure rolls the apply back);
  `provider-auth` and `spoke-connected` wait on the user (`opencode auth login`, starting OpenCode), so by default
  the `verify-harness` step commits OpenCode as installed, not ready (`requireReady: false`, set by `hubctl setup
  apply` unless `--require-ready`). The executor's own default stays strict.
- **Rollback.** All rollback goes through the engine. The new version directory is removed, `current` is restored
  from its backup, and the config is restored from its backup, except when the user changed it after hub wrote it.
  Then it is kept and reported as a conflict (`bootstrap-adapter-opencode-apply.test.ts`).

## Windows (`windows-x64`, Phase 2: session-only)

See `../../PHASE2-CONTRACT.md` for the shared rules. For this adapter:

- **Archive.** The asset is `opencode-windows-x64-baseline.zip`. Baseline is used for the same reason as on the other
  x64 targets, and matches hubctl's own `bun-windows-x64-baseline`. Its only member is `opencode.exe`, zipped on a
  FAT host, so there are no unix modes and the member's kind follows its name. It is installed as
  `data:hub/harnesses/opencode/<version>/bin/opencode.exe`. The unpacker takes the binary name from the
  install-harness action's `target`, so a Windows binary is never installed for a POSIX target, or the other way
  round. A tar.gz is refused for Windows.
- **Release assets (v2.2.0).** `opencode-windows-x64.zip` (118 610 002 bytes, needs AVX2),
  `opencode-windows-x64-baseline.zip` (118 610 005 bytes) and `opencode-windows-arm64.zip`. All three are listed in
  the release's `SHA256SUMS` and in the API's `assets[].digest`.
- **Pin.** The windows-x64 pin (`opencode-windows-x64-baseline.zip`) is reviewed in `../../release/harness-pins.json`
  since 2026-11-06 (checks re-run on a Windows host: release by github-actions[bot], fresh download size and sha256
  equal to `SHA256SUMS` and `assets[].digest`, one member `opencode.exe`; `evidence: []`, the release's only
  attestation is an in-toto release record, not a signature hub checks).
- **MCP authority.** `user-bin:hubctl.exe`, the real executable (`authorityFor`). The `hub` alias is a cmd shim
  (`user-bin:hub.cmd`) on Windows, and a `.cmd` cannot be the MCP command because OpenCode starts it without a
  shell. So `authority: user-bin:hub` is refused on Windows. `.exe` names are refused on POSIX targets.
- **Config path form.** The command is written as the native path (`C:\Users\…\.local\bin\hubctl.exe`, through
  `toNativePath`):
  - CreateProcess would accept `C:/…` too.
  - The native form is what OpenCode's Windows users and docs write, so a user reading the config recognises it.
  - It survives `cmd.exe`, should anything route the command through a shell (`/` starts a switch there).

  Matching is lenient: an existing entry in either separator form and any letter case counts as registered (NTFS is
  case-insensitive). A `hub`/`hubctl` program with `.exe` or `.cmd` at another path counts as stale.
- **Readiness.** The probes run `…/current/bin/opencode.exe`. `nodeProcessRunner` takes a canonical absolute path
  (POSIX or `C:/…`) and passes the OS its native form.

2. Download the asset yourself, then measure and hash it:
   `curl -fsSLo f "$URL" && wc -c < f && shasum -a 256 f`.
3. Cross-check against both upstream values: the asset's line in the release's `SHA256SUMS`, and `assets[].digest`
   from `https://api.github.com/repos/anomalyco/opencode/releases/tags/v<version>`. If any value differs, stop.
4. List the archive and confirm it holds exactly one regular file, `opencode`: `unzip -Z1 f` or `tar -tzvf f`. The
   adapter refuses anything else.
5. Keep `evidence: []`, because OpenCode publishes no signatures. Set `minimumVersion` to `2.0.0`, or higher to
   raise the floor after a security release.
6. Fill in `review` and open the PR. Someone other than the author reviews it (`release/README.md`).

## Integration requirements (HBS-13)

HBS-13 made these edits (`packages/cli/src/setup/`, docs/bootstrap-contracts.md §7): A1 at the composition layer
(refusals become envelope errors), A2 (`setup/dispatch.ts`), the spoke probe (`GET /spoke/presence`), the launchers
(they prefer `~/.local/bin/hubctl`) and A4 (the shared fixtures use `plugins`). A3, A5 and A6 stay open (§7.6).
The original list:

- **Construction.** `packages/cli/src/cli.ts` (setup preview, apply and recover):
  - Build `createOpencodeHarness({ probe: createNodeProbe(), manifest: <verified manifest>, pluginVersion?: <hubctl
    version>, spoke: <SpokeProbe>, installed, floor, allowDowngrade })`.
  - Register `.adapter` in the `AdapterRegistry` passed to **both** `previewSetup` and `revalidateApply`, with
    identical options, so the plan digests match.
- **Refusals.** `planSetup` calls `adapter.plan()`, which **throws `OpencodePlanError`** (`code`: `conflict`,
  `manual_edit_required`, `unpinned_artifact`, `preview_stale` or `invalid`). Catch it around
  `previewSetup`/`revalidateApply` and print it as the envelope error with `exitFor(code)`. Amendment A1 would make
  this unnecessary.
- **Executors.** The `ExecutorMap` holds one executor per kind. `register-mcp-server` and `verify-harness` must
  dispatch on `action.harness` to each adapter's executor: `harness.executors(() => adapterContext)` for OpenCode.
  `builtinExecutors({ harness })` takes one `HarnessSource`, so the integrator needs a source that dispatches on
  `action.harness` (OpenCode: `harness.source`). See A2.
- **Adapter context.** `AdapterContext.env` must be the user's real `process.env`: the provider probe needs the user's
  own provider configuration. `now: Date.now`.
- **Spoke probe.** The hub needs a machine-credential query that answers "is an OpenCode spoke of this machine
  connected?". Today `GET /api/machines` (user auth) lists `processes` per machine. Without a `SpokeProbe`, OpenCode
  is never ready, which is correct; since contract v1.2 it only blocks a strict (`--require-ready`) apply.
- **Authority.** The MCP server runs `user-bin:hubctl`, which this plan's `install-artifact` installs.
  `src/spoke/launchers.ts` writes `hub`/`hubctl` launchers into the hub state dir that run the CLI bundle from the
  plugin's install (cache) directory. They must not become what services or MCP clients depend on. Suggested
  change: when a standalone `user-bin:hubctl` exists, the launchers exec it instead of the bundle.

- **A1.** `HarnessAdapter.plan` returns only `Action[]`, so it cannot report a refusal or findings (drift, unpinned

# Install scripts: shared contract (Phase 1)

Design: `docs/plans/2026-11-05-machine-setup-installer-design.md`. Three workstreams build against this file; change
it only through the integrator.

## Routes (server)

`GET /install.sh` and `GET /install.ps1`: public (no auth), dispatched in `src/central/http.ts` `handle()` before
`/api/`, next to `/.well-known/hub`. Answer `200 text/plain; charset=utf-8`, `cache-control: no-store`,
`x-content-type-options: nosniff`.

Query (every key optional, each at most once; any other key → 400):

| Key | Values | Default | install.ps1 (Phase 3) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `profile` | `session-only` · `launch-node` · `full-harness` | `session-only` | `session-only` · `launch-node`; `full-harness` 400 (no Claude Code / Codex user services on Windows yet) |
| `root` | workspace root for `launch-node`: 1–200 chars of `[A-Za-z0-9._/~-]`, starts with `/` or `~/`, no `..` segment, no `//` | `~/projects` when profile is `launch-node` | starts with `~/` or a drive path `X:/` (one letter, `:`, `/`, forward slashes), then the same allowlist and rules; `/…` is 400. install.sh refuses a drive path |
| `activate` | `0` · `1` | `0` | `0` · `1` |

`root` with another profile → 400. Errors are `400 text/plain` with a one-line reason (no script).

Other answers: `503 text/plain` when this hub has no matching release (see `HUB_RELEASE_BASE`), `400` when the hub's
public URL is plain `http` on a non-private host.

## Template placeholders

Templates are `src/central/install/install.sh` and `src/central/install/install.ps1`, imported as text. The server
replaces every `{{NAME}}` below (each exactly as given; all values are pre-validated and contain none of
`'` `"` `` ` `` `$` `\` newline, so templates put them inside single quotes). An unknown or leftover `{{…}}` is a
server bug (tests check none remain).

| Placeholder | Value |
|---|---|
| `{{HUB_URL}}` | the hub's public origin, no trailing slash (`https://hub.example.com`) |
| `{{HUB_VERSION}}` | the hub version, e.g. `0.8.2` |
| `{{RELEASE_BASE}}` | `https://github.com/huynle/hub-releases/releases/download/v<version>`, or `$HUB_RELEASE_BASE` (server env) when set |
| `{{PROFILE}}` | the profile |
| `{{WORKSPACE_ROOT}}` | the root, or empty |
| `{{ACTIVATE}}` | `0` or `1` |
| `{{INSECURE_HTTP}}` | `1` when `HUB_URL` is `http://` on loopback or a private-network IP, else `0` |

## Script behaviour (scripts workstream)

- All work in a `main` function called on the last line; a truncated download runs nothing.
- `install.sh`: POSIX `sh`. Environment `HUB_INSTALL_RELEASE_BASE`, when set, overrides `{{RELEASE_BASE}}` (tests;
  the local user controls it anyway). Downloads `hubctl-<target>`, `HUBCTL_SHA256SUMS`, `hubctl-manifest.json`.
- `install.ps1`: runs under `irm … | iex`, so it must **never** call `exit` (that closes the user's window): every
  failure is caught at the top, printed as one red `hub setup: …` line, and the function returns (the session stays
  open). Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 both, ASCII only. Phase 2 (`packages/cli/src/bootstrap/PHASE2-CONTRACT.md`):
  x64 only (`PROCESSOR_ARCHITEW6432`, else `PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE`, must be `AMD64`); downloads
  `hubctl-windows-x64.exe`, `HUBCTL_SHA256SUMS`, `hubctl-manifest.json` (`HUB_INSTALL_RELEASE_BASE` overrides, as in
  install.sh; redirects followed, https stays https) into a private temp dir, checks the sha256, then runs install.sh's
  hubctl sequence and exit-code handling with an empty stdin. After a successful apply it adds `<home>\.local\bin` to
  the user PATH when missing (`HKCU\Environment` value read and written unexpanded, keeping its kind; a throwaway
  `SetEnvironmentVariable` user variable is set and cleared to broadcast the change) and to the session's PATH.
  `HUB_INSTALL_USER_PATH_FILE` (tests) stands in for the registry value.

## Web (dialog workstream)

The console builds commands from `me().publicURL` (fallback `location.origin`):

- macOS / Linux: `curl -fsSL '<origin>/install.sh?<query>' | sh`
- Windows: `irm '<origin>/install.ps1?<query>' | iex`

`<query>` uses `URLSearchParams` with defaults left out (no query → bare path); `'` never appears (the allowlists
exclude it).

# Phase 2: hubctl on Windows (session-only), shared contract

Design: `docs/plans/2026-11-05-machine-setup-installer-design.md` §3 (Phase 2). Decision: Brain `1bwf3cqx`. Four
workstreams build against this file in parallel; change it only through the integrator. The foundation below is
already on `feat/ms2` (commit after `bbb8d43a`).

## Foundation (done; do not change without the integrator)

- **Canonical paths** (`contracts/validate.ts` `isAbsolutePath`): POSIX `/a/b` or Windows `C:/a/b` (upper-case drive,
  `/` separators, roots `/` and `C:/`). UNC (`\\server`, `//server`) and device paths (`\\?\`, `\\.\`) are never
  canonical. Contracts, plans, journals and snapshots hold canonical paths only.
- **Edges**: `discovery/util.ts` `normalizeAbs` turns a host's native path into a canonical one (backslashes → `/`,
  drive upper-cased); `contracts/validate.ts` `toNativePath(p, process.platform)` turns it back for external programs
  (icacls, error messages). Node's `fs` accepts canonical `C:/…` paths directly on Windows, so fs calls need no
  conversion. `isWindowsPath(p)` tells them apart. `join` and `resolvePathRef` handle the `C:/` root.
- **Target**: `windows-x64` is in `SUPPORTED_TARGETS` with `platform: "windows"`, `libc: "none"`,
  `serviceManager: "none"` (type `TargetServiceManager`), `bunTarget: "bun-windows-x64-baseline"`. `windows-arm64`
  stays unsupported. `targetOf("win32", "x64", "none")` is `windows-x64`.

## Windows host layout (all workstreams)

Same XDG-style layout under the user's profile as on macOS/Linux (it is what OpenCode itself uses on Windows):

| Root | Windows path |
|---|---|
| `home` | `%USERPROFILE%` (canonical, e.g. `C:/Users/dacra`); `HOME` wins when set and absolute |
| `config` | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `home/.config` |
| `state` | as today (`resolveHubStateDir`), else `home/.local/state` |
| `data` | `$XDG_DATA_HOME` or `home/.local/share` |
| `user-bin` | `home/.local/bin` (install.ps1 adds it to the user PATH) |
| `system-bin`, `launch-agents`, `systemd-user` | not mapped on Windows |

Executables on `windows-x64` carry `.exe` in their PathRefs (`user-bin:hubctl.exe`, harness `…/bin/opencode.exe`).

## Install primitives on win32 (transaction workstream implements; adapters/planner rely on them)

- **`link-executable`** (the `hub` alias, `opencode` on PATH): on win32 the planner names the link
  `user-bin:<name>.cmd` and the applier writes a **cmd shim** instead of a symlink: exactly
  `@"<native target>" %*\r\n` (ASCII). Journaled as a file it owns; rollback removes/restores it. No symlinks for
  executables on Windows (they need Developer Mode or admin).
- **Directory "current" links** (`select-harness` and friends): an NTFS **junction** (`fs.symlinkSync(target, path,
  "junction")`), no admin needed. `lstat` reports junctions as symbolic links, so `checkNoSymlinkEscape` still refuses
  to write *through* one.
- **Replacing a file that may be running** (`hubctl.exe` while OpenCode runs `hubctl mcp`): rename-aside: move the old
  file to `<name>.old-<txid>` in the same directory, move the staged file in, delete the aside file when possible
  (else leave it; a later apply or `setup recover` cleans `*.old-*`). Rollback renames back. Names are
  `<name>.old-<txID>-<seq>` (`-undo` during a rollback). When the aside is the running hubctl.exe itself (a rollback
  that removes hubctl), `setup rollback`/`recover` start a hidden `cmd.exe` with a fixed command line that deletes it
  once it is no longer running (`setup/self-aside.ts`).
- **`O_NOFOLLOW`** is undefined on Windows: replace it with an explicit `lstat` reparse-point check right before the
  open, and refuse links.
- **File modes**: Windows has no POSIX modes. Journals record `mode: null` ("not applicable") for win32 entries;
  comparisons skip it. The machine credential and other secret files get an owner-only ACL instead (next section).

## Secrets on win32 (transaction workstream)

Files that are 0600 on POSIX (`config.json` with the machine token, `cli.json`, preview files with tokens) are, on
win32, created empty, restricted with `icacls <native> /inheritance:r /grant:r *<current user SID>:(F)` **before** the
secret is written, then moved into place (the ACL travels with the move). Checks that today refuse `mode & 0o077`
(e.g. `packages/node/src/opencode-warm.ts:323`) instead verify on win32 that the ACL has no allow entry for anyone but
the current user, SYSTEM and Administrators. Keep a small helper (`win-acl.ts`) both sides import; tests inject the
`icacls` runner.

## Profiles on a target without services

`session-only` works on `windows-x64`. `launch-node` and `full-harness` are refused at preview with
`unsupported_platform` and the message "needs user services, which hubctl does not install on Windows yet". The
server (`/install.ps1`) and the console already allow only `session-only` on Windows.

## install.ps1 (scripts workstream)

Switches from the plugin path to hubctl, mirroring install.sh: download `hubctl-windows-x64.exe`,
`HUBCTL_SHA256SUMS`, `hubctl-manifest.json` from `{{RELEASE_BASE}}` (env `HUB_INSTALL_RELEASE_BASE` overrides, as in
install.sh), check the sha256 with `Get-FileHash`, then `machine status --json` / `machine enroll --server …
[--allow-insecure-http]` / `setup preview --profile session-only --enrollment separate --manifest … --out …` /
`setup apply` / `setup verify` with install.sh's exit-code handling (15 → done with next steps; 10 → manual edits),
and finally add `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin` to the user PATH (`[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('Path', …,
'User')`, only when missing) and say to open a new terminal. Never `exit`; ASCII only; PowerShell 5.1 and 7.

## Release (release workstream)

`hubctl-windows-x64.exe` is built (`--target bun-windows-x64-baseline`, `.exe` outfile), listed in the manifest and
`HUBCTL_SHA256SUMS`, and smoke-tested on `windows-latest` in `release.yml`. The OpenCode harness pin for
`windows-x64` follows the reviewed-pin process (`release/README.md`): the agent may prepare the entry with a
re-downloaded digest, but the `review` block must be filled in by the owner (flag it, never self-review).
A local **dev release** script builds hubctl for chosen targets with a throwaway trust root and signs a manifest with
a throwaway key, so the integrator can test on real machines through `HUB_RELEASE_BASE` without the release key.

# Phase 3: user services on Windows (launch-node), shared contract

Design: `docs/plans/2026-11-05-machine-setup-installer-design.md` §3 (Phase 3); Phase 2 contract
`PHASE2-CONTRACT.md` and `docs/bootstrap-contracts.md` §11 (v1.3) still hold. Branch `feat/ms3` from v0.8.7
(`ebe8f6a1`). Three workstreams build against this file in parallel; change it only through the integrator.

Goal: `launch-node` works on `windows-x64`. `hub node` runs as a per-user logon task (no admin, no password, no
visible window), the node keeps OpenCode's background service running so the machine stays online without OpenCode
open, and launches prepare worktrees under `C:/…` workspace roots. `full-harness` (Claude Code / Codex spokes) stays
refused on Windows (Phase 4).

## Paths in the protocol and the node (workstream A)

- The launch/node protocol (`packages/protocol/src/launch.ts` `isAbsolutePath`, `node.ts`) accepts canonical absolute
  paths exactly as the bootstrap contracts do: POSIX `/a/b` or Windows `C:/a/b` (upper-case drive, `/`, no UNC or
  device paths). Reuse or mirror `packages/cli/src/bootstrap/contracts/validate.ts` `isAbsolutePath` (one rule).
- Everything the node sends (hello `workspaceRoots`, prepared `directory`) is canonical; the node canonicalizes
  native paths it reads (node.json, `realpathSync`, git output) at the edge (`normalizeAbs`-style). The hub compares
  canonical strings; drive letters are upper-case, so case-insensitive Windows paths compare equal.
- node.json `workspaceRoots` on Windows may be written as `C:\Users\x\projects`, `C:/Users/x/projects` or
  `~/projects`; the node canonicalizes them.

## The `task-scheduler` service manager (workstream B)

- `ServiceManager` gains `"task-scheduler"`; `windows-x64` has `serviceManager: "task-scheduler"` (was `"none"`).
  Discovery reports `task-scheduler` on Windows when `%SystemRoot%\System32\schtasks.exe` exists, else `none`.
- New root `task-defs` = `state/hub/tasks` (canonical `C:/Users/x/.local/state/hub/tasks`): where hubctl writes the
  rendered Task XML it registers. The XML is journaled like a unit file; Task Scheduler keeps its own copy.
- Embedded asset `service/task-scheduler/node` = `scripts/hub-node.task.xml`, kind `task-xml`. The rendered file is
  written as **UTF-16LE with BOM** if `schtasks /XML` needs it (verify on Windows; UTF-8 if it accepts that).
- Task: name `hub-node-<user>` (user = `%USERNAME%`, `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` only, others `_`) in the root folder;
  `LogonTrigger` for this user; principal = the user's SID, `InteractiveToken`, `LeastPrivilege` (no admin, no stored
  password); `MultipleInstancesPolicy` `IgnoreNew`; no battery limits; `ExecutionTimeLimit` `PT0S`;
  `RestartOnFailure` interval `PT1M`, count `999`. No visible window: the action must not open a console window at
  logon (try `conhost.exe --headless <hubctl.exe> node run`; if that is not reliable, find another way, verify it on
  Windows, and say what you chose). The command is `user-bin:hubctl.exe node run` (native path in the XML), never a
  `.cmd`.
- No per-task environment exists: settings a systemd unit carries in `Environment=` are passed another way (flags, or
  nothing when they are defaults). The script layout (`__RUNTIME__ __ENTRY__`) is refused on Windows: only the
  standalone `hubctl.exe` layout.
- Control: absolute `%SystemRoot%\System32\schtasks.exe`, `shell:false`, `windowsHide:true`, a fixed allowlist:
  `/Create /TN <name> /XML <abs task-defs file> /F`, `/Run /TN <name>`, `/End /TN <name>`, `/Delete /TN <name> /F`,
  `/Query /TN <name> /XML` (state: registered / enabled) and a locale-independent running check (e.g. the task's
  process: `hubctl.exe` with `node run` whose parent is the Task Scheduler engine, or `schtasks /Query /XML` plus a
  CIM process query) with the same `state` / `activate` / `deactivate` / `restore` / `health` semantics and the
  existing health window. `/End` is TerminateProcess: no graceful stop on Windows (accepted; the node is crash-safe).
- Exit 78 ("nothing to do") cannot be excluded from restarts in Task XML: on win32 the node exits **0** in that case
  (no restart) and logs why; the task is started again at the next logon or by `hubctl setup apply`.
- The hand path `hub node install/uninstall` on Windows writes the XML and prints the `schtasks` commands (never runs
  them), like launchd/systemd today.
- Profiles: `launch-node` plans on `windows-x64`; `full-harness` stays refused there with
  "<service> needs a user service hubctl does not install on Windows yet" for the claude-code / codex spokes.
  `--workspace-root` takes native or canonical Windows paths and `~/…`.

## The node on Windows (workstream A)

- **OpenCode background service.** On win32, when no background service is registered or its process is gone, the node
  starts it (`<opencode> service start`, found like the warmer finds OpenCode, `windowsHide`, no shell), at most once
  per tick with back-off, and logs it. Then the warmer warms it as on other OSes. Verify on Windows where OpenCode
  2.x writes `service.json` and how `opencode service start` behaves; fix `run.ts`'s path if it differs.
- `opencode-warm.ts` `readServiceRegistration`: the POSIX mode check (`mode & 0o022`) does not apply on win32; use the
  ACL check from `src/win-acl.ts` (owner, SYSTEM, Administrators only) or none for a non-secret file — say which.
- Process trees: `git.ts` (and `runtime-openshell/src/cli.ts` if it can run on Windows) stop with the shared
  `packages/cli/src/bootstrap/adapters/process-tree.ts` tree kill on win32 instead of `process.kill(-pid)`.
- Harness lookup (`harnesses.ts`): PATHEXT and `.exe` on win32 (`opencode.exe`, `claude.exe`, `bin/codex.exe`).
- Every spawn that can run on Windows sets `windowsHide: true` (also `control.ts` `defaultSpawn`,
  `claude-code/src/wrapper.ts`, `codex/src/wrapper.ts`).

## Installer and console (workstream C)

- `/install.ps1` accepts `profile=launch-node`, `root` and `activate=1` (still refuses `full-harness`). `root` on

`ssh winpixel` (user `dacra`, PowerShell 5.1 remote shell; send scripts as `powershell -NoProfile -EncodedCommand

## As built (integrator, 2026-11-06)

Verified on winpixel during the workstreams; these replace the contract text where they differ.

- **Encoding:** `schtasks /XML` refuses UTF-8 ("unable to switch the encoding"); the Task XML is written UTF-16LE
  with a BOM.
- **No window:** the action is `conhost.exe --headless <hubctl.exe> node run` (checked with Comet KVM screenshots
  and a window-process query; without `--headless` Windows Terminal opens).
- **Restart:** `conhost --headless` always exits 0, so `RestartOnFailure` never fires. The logon trigger repeats every
  minute with `IgnoreNew`: an exited node is started again within a minute whatever its exit code.
- **Idle node:** because of that, a node with no workspace roots on win32 does not exit: it logs why and re-reads
  node.json every 60 s (`IDLE_RECHECK_MS`) until it lists roots (replaces "exit 0").
- **Logs:** stderr is lost under the headless console, so on win32 `hub node run` also appends to
  `<hub state dir>/node.log` (rotated to `node.log.1` past 1 MiB).
- **Stop:** `schtasks /End` ends only the console host; deactivate first runs `taskkill /T /F /PID <pid>` on the
  task's process (allowlisted as exactly that), then `/End` and `/Delete`.
- **Running check:** a fixed PowerShell script reads the task through Task Scheduler's COM API (numeric state, so no
  localized text, and the action's process ID).
- **Carried settings:** variables a systemd unit would carry (`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` …) are dropped on Windows and named in
  a warning at preview and `hub node install`.
- **Spokes:** `full-harness` is refused per spoke ("claude-code needs a user service hubctl does not install on Windows
  yet", likewise codex-spoke).
- **Node paths:** service.json is `%USERPROFILE%\.local\state\opencode\service.json` (as on POSIX); it is checked by ACL.
  Launch placement compares canonical paths exactly (drive upper-case); a repo path differing only in case from a
  node's root is not placed there.
